_notes: Use with simple case-insensitive substring/word-boundary matching, not exact-match only.
A hit should FLAG the listing for mod review, not auto-reject it — false positives will happen.
For general profanity/slurs, don't hand-roll a list: use an existing, maintained open-source
profanity filter library (e.g. a package like 'profanity-filter' / 'bad-words' for your bot's
language, or a maintained list like LDNOOBW) instead of the categories below. Those libraries
are kept current and cover slurs/obscenity properly; this file only covers ARC Raiders-specific
ToS and marketplace risk language, which no generic library will catch.
Review and expand this list periodically — community slang for RMT/boosting evolves quickly
and often uses deliberate misspellings to dodge filters (e.g. 'p ay pal', 'c4shapp').
Each category has an "action": "hold" = a mod must approve before the job posts;
"notify" = the job posts right away and #mod-review gets a heads-up with a Take down button.
Move a term between categories to change how strictly it is handled.

real_money_trading.description: Signals someone is offering/requesting items, currency, or accounts for real money — banned per ARC Raiders' EULA/ToS.

account_trading_and_sharing.description: Selling, buying, or sharing ARC Raiders accounts/credentials — explicitly banned per Embark's support FAQ.

boosting_and_carrying.description: Paid or guaranteed-outcome carry/boost services — the exact ambiguity your job board is designed to avoid; flags it for a human to confirm it's framed as co-op play, not a paid carry.

cheating_and_exploits.description: References to cheats, hacks, or exploits — a job board post mentioning these is a serious red flag regardless of context.

scams.description: Phishing / fake giveaway bait. Always held.

trade_talk.description: Ordinary trading words that are usually about in-game items, not real money. Posted, but mods get a heads-up in case it turns out to be RMT.

low_effort_or_spam_signals.description: Not banned language, just quality/legitimacy signals — pair with a length/emoji-ratio check rather than a pure word match.
